# Cold Case to Published: The Complete System for Writing, Legally Protecting, and Self-Publishing Your True Crime Ebook in 90 Days

### A Fill-in-the-Scaffold Template Pack

---

## FULL TABLE OF CONTENTS

---

**WELCOME SECTION**
- How This System Works (And Why It's Built for Obsessive Researchers Like You)
- The 90-Day Roadmap at a Glance
- What's Included: Your Complete Template Pack Inventory

---

**MODULE 1: CASE COMMAND CENTER**
*Getting Your Research Out of Your Head and Into a System*

- 1.1 — The Cold Case Master File: How to Build Your Central Research Hub
- 1.2 — **[TEMPLATE 1] Case Master Timeline Spreadsheet** *(Fill-in-the-Scaffold)*
  - Tab 1: Chronological Event Log
  - Tab 2: Person of Interest Tracker
  - Tab 3: Physical Evidence Inventory
  - Tab 4: Media Coverage Log
  - Tab 5: Unresolved Questions Parking Lot
- 1.3 — **[TEMPLATE 2] Source Credibility Tracker** *(Fill-in-the-Scaffold)*
  - Primary vs. Secondary vs. Tertiary Source Tiers
  - Reliability Scoring Matrix
  - "Quote or Paraphrase?" Decision Guide
- 1.4 — The Reddit Thread Problem: How to Process Forum Speculation Without Poisoning Your Manuscript
- 1.5 — **[TEMPLATE 3] FOIA Request Swipe File** *(Copy-Paste Ready)*
  - Federal FOIA Request Letter
  - State Public Records Request Letter (Adaptable Template)
  - Law Enforcement Records Request Letter
  - Medical Examiner / Coroner Records Request
  - Follow-Up and Appeal Letter Templates
  - FOIA Tracking Log

---

**MODULE 2: STORY ARCHITECTURE**
*Transforming Raw Research Into a Narrative People Cannot Put Down*

- 2.1 — Why True Crime Fails on the Page (And What Separates the Bestsellers from the Abandoned Drafts)
- 2.2 — Choosing Your Narrative Lens: Five Structural Models for Cold Case Books
  - The Chronological Unraveling
  - The Investigator's Journey (You as Narrator)
  - The Victim-First Model
  - The Community Portrait
  - The Multi-Perspective Mosaic
- 2.3 — **[TEMPLATE 4] Chapter-by-Chapter Narrative Outline Template** *(Fill-in-the-Scaffold)*
  - Universal Cold Case Chapter Framework (12 Chapters + Epilogue)
  - Chapter Purpose Statement Prompts
  - Scene-Level Beat Sheet per Chapter
  - Transition Bridge Prompts Between Chapters
- 2.4 — The Opening Hook Formula: Three Proven Cold Case Opening Strategies With Examples
- 2.5 — Writing the Victim as a Human Being, Not a Case File
- 2.6 — Handling Gaps, Unknowns, and Contradictions in Your Narrative
- 2.7 — Pacing Your Evidence: When to Reveal What
- 2.8 — The Ending Problem: How to Close a Case That Was Never Solved
- 2.9 — Voice and Tone Guide: Finding the Register Between Sensational and Clinical

---

**MODULE 3: THE LEGAL SAFETY SYSTEM**
*What You Can Write, What You Can't, and How to Stay Protected*

- 3.1 — The Fear Is Real But Manageable: A Plain-English Overview of Your Legal Exposure as a Self-Published True Crime Author
- 3.2 — **[TEMPLATE 5] The True Crime Legal Review Checklist** *(Plain-English, Self-Administered)*
  - Section A: Defamation Risk Assessment
  - Section B: Privacy Law Considerations (Public vs. Private Figures)
  - Section C: Naming Living Suspects and Persons of Interest
  - Section D: Victims, Families, and Minor Children
  - Section E: Using Photographs, Documents, and Court Exhibits
  - Section F: Social Media Content and Forum

listing.title: Cold Case to Published: The Complete System for Writing, Legally Protecting, and Self-Publishing Your True Crime Ebook in 90 Days
listing.tagline: Turn your scattered cold case research into a published Kindle ebook — with the templates, narrative structure, and plain-English legal guardrails you need to do it confidently and safely.
listing.description: You've spent months down the rabbit hole. You have browser tabs, Google Docs, Reddit threads, court records, and a head full of theories — but every time you sit down to actually write the ebook, you freeze. How do you turn hundreds of disjointed notes into a story someone actually wants to read? What order do the chapters go in? And the question that quietly terrifies you: can you legally name that suspect, that detective, that still-living person of interest without getting sued? Cold Case to Published is the only system built specifically for true crime researchers like you that solves all three of those problems in one place — without making you take a $300 course, hire an attorney, or figure it out alone.
listing.description2: This is a fill-in-the-scaffold template pack, not a lecture. You get a Case Master Timeline Spreadsheet to collapse your scattered research into a single chronological source of truth, a Chapter-by-Chapter Narrative Outline Template modeled on the structure of bestselling true crime books, a Source Credibility Tracker so you always know what you can cite and what you can't, a FOIA Request Swipe File with ready-to-send language for requesting police records, autopsy reports, and court documents, and a plain-English Legal Review Checklist that walks you through defamation risk, privacy considerations, and the specific rules around naming suspects, persons of interest, and living individuals in self-published work — written so a non-lawyer can actually use it.
listing.description3: Every other product you've found owns only one lane. The Gumroad toolkit organizes research but says nothing about how to write. The Udemy course teaches narrative craft but never mentions what happens when you publish someone's name. The Amazon ebook addresses legal anxiety but leaves you with no structure for turning your notes into chapters. This pack bridges all three gaps because a true crime writer who is organized but legally exposed, or legally cautious but narratively lost, never actually publishes. You will. Within 90 days, you can go from a folder of chaos to a finished, formatted, published ebook on Kindle — and you'll know exactly what you wrote, why it's structured the way it is, and why you're protected.
bulletPoints: Case Master Timeline Spreadsheet: drag every date, source, witness, and event into one organized document so you never lose track of what happened when or where you found it

Chapter-by-Chapter Narrative Outline Template: follow the proven structural scaffold used in bestselling true crime books — hook, background, investigation arc, suspect analysis, resolution or open verdict — so your ebook reads like a real book, not a Wikipedia article

Source Credibility Tracker: categorize every piece of evidence by reliability, citeability, and legal sensitivity so you know exactly what belongs in your manuscript and what stays in your private notes

FOIA Request Swipe File: copy-paste letter templates for requesting police reports, 911 call logs, autopsy records, and court documents from local, state, and federal agencies — with guidance on following up when they ignore you

Plain-English Legal Review Checklist: a step-by-step self-audit covering defamation, false light, privacy invasion, and the specific rules for naming suspects, persons of interest, and living individuals — so you publish with confidence instead of second-guessing every sentence
listing.callToAction: Get instant access to every template, checklist, and swipe file — and start turning your cold case obsession into a published ebook today.
